blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Managing last-mile delivery is managing a thousand tiny problems at the same time. A customer gives the wrong address. A flat number is missing. A gate is locked. A driver's handheld device crashes. A dog bites. A neighbour refuses to sign. Each one is small; together, they are the whole job.

Experienced last-mile managers win by building simple, repeatable responses to each of the common problems, so that the driver never has to invent a solution on the doorstep. The customer service team knows what to say when the parcel is re-attempted. The dispatcher knows which address issues need a phone call before the van leaves, not after the van returns.

Nobody said that small flat numbers would be fun. They said there would be a thousand of them, every single day.

items.q: According to the text, what makes last-mile delivery hard?
options: A thousand tiny problems at the same time
items.why: "Managing last-mile delivery is managing a thousand tiny problems at the same time."

items.q: How do experienced managers win, according to the text?
options: By letting drivers improvise on the doorstep
By building simple, repeatable responses to common problems
By hiring more drivers for each route
items.why: "win by building simple, repeatable responses… so that the driver never has to invent a solution on the doorstep."

items.q: When should the dispatcher handle an address issue?
options: With a phone call before the van leaves
items.why: "which address issues need a phone call before the van leaves, not after the van returns."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: The dispatcher can prevent problems before the van leaves.
Many small failures add up to the whole job.
A good driver is one who invents a clever fix at each door.
Standard responses make the job more manageable.
items.why: Inferência: o texto defende respostas pré-construídas justamente para que o motorista NÃO precise improvisar na porta.

items.q: The final line about the flat numbers suggests that…
options: the job is easy but boring
the difficulty is the sheer volume, not any single case
no one expected the work to be repetitive
flat numbers are the only real problem
items.why: Inferência: "a thousand of them, every single day" — o desafio é a escala e a repetição, não um caso isolado.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie explicando o novo manual de respostas para a equipe. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, so here's what I've built. Ten cards, one for each problem we hit every single day — locked gate, missing flat number, dog on the property, dead handheld, neighbour won't sign. Each card tells the driver exactly what to do, word for word. No thinking on the doorstep.

Yesterday one of the drivers told me he'd spent twenty minutes at a gate, ringing three different flats, hoping someone would buzz him in. Twenty minutes, one parcel. That's the cost of improvising. So the card for a locked gate now says: try the buzzer once, send the pre-written text, and move on. We re-attempt tomorrow.

Here's the important part. The address problems don't belong to the driver at all — they belong to the dispatcher. If a flat number is missing, we call the customer before the van leaves the depot, not after it comes back empty. That one change alone should cut our failed deliveries.

And please, when something new comes up that isn't on a card, tell me straight away. Small problems grow fast. I'd rather write a new card tonight than lose a hundred parcels next week.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What has Sophie built for the team?
options: A new routing app for the vans
Ten cards, one for each daily problem
A training video for new drivers
items.why: "Ten cards, one for each problem we hit every single day."

items.q: What does the card for a locked gate now tell the driver to do?
options: Return the parcel to the depot immediately
Try the buzzer once, send the text, and move on
Wait until someone buzzes them in
Ring every flat until it works
items.why: "try the buzzer once, send the pre-written text, and move on. We re-attempt tomorrow."

items.q: Who does Sophie say the address problems belong to?
items.why: "The address problems don't belong to the driver at all — they belong to the dispatcher."

items.q: Why does Sophie mention the driver who spent twenty minutes at a gate?
options: To show how patient the drivers are
To argue that gates should be removed
To illustrate the cost of improvising without a standard response
items.why: Inferência: ela usa o caso como exemplo de desperdício — "That's the cost of improvising."

items.q: What can we infer about why Sophie wants to hear about new problems immediately?
options: She enjoys writing cards at night
She does not trust the drivers to solve anything
Acting early prevents a small issue from becoming a large loss
She wants to reduce the number of dispatchers
items.why: Inferência: "Small problems grow fast… I'd rather write a new card tonight than lose a hundred parcels next week."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The driver waited at the gate because the code didn't work." A gate is…
options: a barrier or entrance you pass through
items.why: Gate = portão, a barreira ou entrada da propriedade.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The scanner ___ mid-route, so we lost every proof of delivery for the afternoon."
items.why: To crash = travar; o aparelho parou de funcionar no meio da rota.

items.q: "We will re-attempt the parcel tomorrow." To re-attempt means to…
items.why: To re-attempt = tentar a entrega de novo.

items.q: Dispatcher is best described as the person who…
options: packs the boxes in the warehouse
coordinates routes and address issues from the depot
items.why: Dispatcher = expedidor: quem organiza as rotas e resolve os problemas de endereço antes da saída.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Without the ___ number, the driver had no way of knowing which door in the building was correct."
items.why: Flat number = número do apartamento; sem ele não dá para achar a porta certa no prédio.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns em operações de entrega. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Let's roll out the new response cards to every depot next month." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, colocar em operação.

items.q: "The operations lead still has to sign off on the new dispatch rule." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "A couple of drivers pushed back on the 'buzzer once, then move on' rule." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "When a new problem appears, we need to escalate it fast." To escalate a problem means to…
options: raise it to someone with more authority to act
write it in the daily log only
items.why: Escalate = escalar: levar o problema a quem tem alçada para resolvê-lo.

items.q: "The team agreed the new process but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.
